$$[L:F] = [F(\sqrt{-7}):F]\cdot[F(\sqrt{-7},\alpha):F(\sqrt{-7})]\cdot[L:F(\sqrt{-7},\alpha)] = 2\cdot 2\cdot 2 = 8,$$

The four roots $\alpha,-\alpha,\beta,-\beta$ come in pairs $\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$ and $\{\beta,-\beta\}$. Any $\sigma\in\mathrm{Gal}(L/F)$ permutes the roots and satisfies $\sigma(-\alpha)=-\sigma(\alpha)$, so the induced permutation preserves this pairing. The group of permutations of four elements preserving a fixed pairing into two pairs has order $8$ and is isomorphic to $D_8$ (it is the symmetry group of a "square" with vertices $\alpha,\beta,-\alpha,-\beta$ in cyclic order). Since $\mathrm{Gal}(L/F)$ embeds into this group and $|\mathrm{Gal}(L/F)|=8=|D_8|$, we conclude
$$\mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q}(i))\cong D_8.$$

Thus such a Galois extension exists. $\blacksquare$
